title: Welsh Rarebit
subtitle: Grilled cheddar sauce on toast with mustard and Worcestershire
excerpt: A thick, glossy cheddar sauce made with a light roux and egg yolks, seasoned with Worcestershire sauce and mustard, then grilled on toast until bubbling and brown. Better than cheese on toast in every way.
sourceNotes: Welsh rarebit has been a British staple since at least the 18th century. Despite the name, it contains no rabbit. The word rarebit is thought to be a corruption of rabbit, once a term for a simple peasant dish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made up to 2 days ahead, refrigerated, and spread cold on toast before grilling.
recipe.temperatureNote: Use the grill setting on your oven for the final stage

content.text: Keep the heat low when making the sauce. Too much heat will cause the cheese to split and go greasy rather than smooth and glossy.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the flour and whisk for 1 minute to make a smooth paste.
Gradually add the milk, whisking constantly, until smooth and thickened. This takes about 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the grated cheddar a handful at a time until fully melted.
Stir in the mustard, Worcestershire sauce and paprika.
Beat in the egg yolks quickly. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Toast thick slices of bread. Spread the rarebit sauce generously over each slice.
Place under a hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Cheese sauce is grainy and oily.
items.cause: Heat too high when cheese was added or cheese added all at once.
items.fix: Add cheese off the heat in small batches, stirring each time.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thick to spread.
items.cause: Too much flour or reduced too long.
items.fix: Stir in a splash of milk to loosen.

items.symptom: Rarebit slips off the toast under the grill.
items.cause: Toast was not firm enough or sauce too thin.
items.fix: Toast bread until fully dry before spreading; chill sauce briefly if it is very runny.
